title: Reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, and backpressure
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming token generation has a non-trivial per-token overhead that shows up on p50 and especially p95 latencies for short token bursts. This PR reduces per-token overhead by reworking the token loop, improving flush cadence, and adding a light-weight backpressure signal between the network sender and the token generator worker. Highlights: 1) Token loop refactor: reduced allocations and branch mispredictions in the hot path, introduced a small per-worker fast-path for 1-token and 2-token continuations, and hoisted common invariants out of the inner loop. 2) Flush cadence: introduce configurable flush_cadence_ms (default 8ms) with adaptive early-flush when micro-batches reach threshold; reduces tail latency for interactive workloads. 3) Backpressure signaling: lightweight ring-buffer-based credit system so the sender communicates available socket send-buffer space to the generator; prevents large flushes from blocking the token loop and allows the runtime to prefer smaller flushes under pressure. 4) KV cache read path: added a lock-free read path for read-mostly accesses (optimistic snapshot + validation) which reduces blocking when multiple token generators probe the KV cache concurrently. 5) Scheduling tweaks: micro-batch prioritization for streaming requests with small sequence lengths and short TTL; scheduler now favors low-latency lanes for streaming sessions. 6) Kernel invocation batching: avoid creating full-size kernel batches when most examples in the batch are single-token continuations; fall back to a compact batch codepath that issues a smaller kernel with contiguous buffers to the CUDA backend. Results: internal perf lab (V100 and A100 mixes) shows median token-gen latency reduction of ~10% and p95 improvements of 25-40% for interactive streaming workloads (payloads of 1-8 tokens per write). For high-throughput batching workloads there is neutral to small regressions (<3%) in aggregate throughput but improved latency SLO compliance for streaming endpoints. Changes are backwards-compatible and gated behind a runtime flag (runtime.streaming_optimizations=true). Checklist: - [x] Token loop refactor and microbenchmarks - [x] Flush cadence implementation + adaptive logic - [x] Backpressure credit protocol + unit tests - [x] KV cache optimistic read path with validation - [x] Scheduler heuristics and integration tests - [x] End-to-end perf runs + docs and release notes - [x] Feature-flag gating and telemetry - [x] Rollout plan (canary -> gradual) Breaking changes: none. Rollout: start with canary for dedicated pools and hosted streaming v2 routes for 48h with metrics guardrails (p50/p95 token latency, socket errors, backlog); automatic rollback on regressed token latency >10% sustained for 10m.

changed_snippets: runtime/token_loop.cpp: reduced branching in hot loop and replaced std::vector allocations with small_buffer optimization; added fast-path for small continuation sizes
runtime/streaming/flush_controller.cpp: new adaptive flush cadence with early-flush when micro-batch-size >= 4 or latency budget exceeded
runtime/streaming/backpressure_ring.cpp: lightweight ring buffer credits and non-blocking handshake between sender and generator
runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_optimistic.h: optimistic snapshot + validation on reads to avoid locking on common paths
runtime/kernel_batcher.cpp: compact_batch path that packs small-token continuations into contiguous GPU buffers

Maya Patel (2026-02-21): Added microbench numbers to the PR description and introduced telemetry.runtime.streaming.early_flush_count; microbench shows ~12% p50 and ~30% p95 improvement for 1-2 token workloads.

Oliver Smith (2026-02-22): Need to be careful with the optimistic KV read path, please ensure we don't miss revalidation on concurrent writes. Also add a stress test that mutates the KV cache while generators read.
Maya Patel (2026-02-23): Added revalidation and a stress test (tests/kv_cache/optimistic_stress_test.py). We conservatively fallback to locked path on validation failure.
Ravi Desai (2026-02-24): CI flaked on a networking test in the first run; reran. Approving once CI is green. Also suggest a gradual rollout note for Dedicated capacity (added to docs).
Jae Kim (2026-02-25): Approved after addressing comments and adding metrics. Left a minor nit on naming (flush_cadence_ms -> streaming_flush_ms) which I don't think needs blocking follow-up.
Maya Patel (2026-02-26): Renamed config to streaming_flush_ms (backwards-compatible alias kept) and pushed final perf numbers and canary run plan.
Oliver Smith (2026-02-27): LGTM, confirming that both V100 and A100 runs were included in the perf doc. Merging when CI completes.
ci_checks: streaming-perf-harness (flaky): first run failed (socket timeout), rerun -> pass
perf_results: lab/A100: p50 token-latency reduced from 12.8ms -> 11.6ms (~9%), p95 reduced from 54.2ms -> 32.6ms (~40%) for interactive 1-8 token bursts
lab/V100: p50 token-latency reduced from 18.1ms -> 16.2ms (~10.5%), p95 reduced from 78ms -> 55.2ms (~29%)
throughput impact: <3% regression on large-batch throughput in pathological cases; neutral on typical batched workloads
rollout_plan: Gate behind runtime.streaming_optimizations (default: off for existing clusters)
Canary: enable for 5% of hosted streaming v2 routes and one dedicated pool for 48h
Metrics guardrails: token_gen_p50, token_gen_p95, socket_error_rate, backlog_size; auto-rollback on sustained token_gen_p95 regression > 10% for 10 minutes
Gradual unroll to 50% -> 100% over 3 days if no regressions
release_notes: Reduced streaming token-generation latency via token-loop optimizations, adaptive flush cadence, backpressure credits, and KV cache read-path improvements
Default behavior is behind a runtime flag; admins can enable per-cluster
Improved p95 latencies for interactive workloads; minor throughput impact in a few large-batch cases
